## Check the model applcapbility and quality of output


```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)

source("setup.R")
US_Data <- read_csv("Output/1. SOC_Cinput_EF_US_Agg.csv") %>%
  mutate(Region = STATE) %>%
  select(-STATE)

CA_Data <- read_csv("Output/1. SOC_Cinput_EF_Canada_Agg.csv")

Result <- rbind(US_Data, CA_Data) %>%
  mutate(Region = case_when(
    Region == "AB"     ~ "ALBERTA",
    Region == "AT"     ~ "ATLANTIC",
    Region == "BC"     ~ "BRITISH COLUMBIA",
    Region == "MB"     ~ "MANITOBA",
    Region == "QC"     ~ "QUEBEC",
    Region == "SK"     ~ "SASKATCHEWAN",
    Region == "ON"     ~ "ONTARIO",
    TRUE               ~ Region
  ))



 
```

## draw maps to see the SOC change across North America

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(sf)
library(rnaturalearth)
library(rnaturalearthhires)   # high-res polygons

Result <- rbind(US_Data, CA_Data)

# ───────────────────────── 1. polygons ─────────────────────────────
na_states <- ne_states(returnclass = "sf") %>%           # provinces + states
  filter(admin %in% c("United States of America", "Canada")) %>%
  select(name = name_en, postal, geometry)

# ───────────────────────── 2. tidy keys ────────────────────────────
us_lookup <- tibble(
  Region = toupper(state.name),   # full state names → upper-case
  postal = state.abb
)

Result_state_prepped <- Result %>%                # your data
  mutate(Region = toupper(Region)) %>%                  # same case as lookup
  left_join(us_lookup, by = "Region") %>%               # add postal codes
  mutate(postal = coalesce(postal, Region)) %>%         # CA codes already okay
  group_by(postal) %>%                                  # just in case duplicates
  summarise(SOC_predict_wavg = mean(SOC_predict_wavg, na.rm = TRUE),
            .groups = "drop")

# ───────────────────────── 3. join polygons + data ─────────────────
plot_data <- na_states %>%
  left_join(Result_state_prepped, by = "postal")

# ───────────────────────── 4. draw map ─────────────────────────────
soc_map <- ggplot(plot_data) +
  geom_sf(aes(fill = SOC_predict_wavg), colour = "grey70", size = 0.1) +
  scale_fill_gradient2(
    name     = "ΔSOC (t ha⁻¹)",
    low      = "#00008B",  # deep blue  (losses)
    mid      = "#ADD8E6",  # light blue (≈0)
    high     = "#FFFF00",  # yellow     (gains)
    midpoint = 0,
    na.value = "white"     # no data
  ) +
  coord_sf(crs = 3347) +   # Canada Albers equal-area
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(
    panel.grid.major = element_blank(),
    legend.position  = "right"
  )

print(soc_map)

# ───────────────────────── 5. save file ────────────────────────────
ggsave("Figures/SOC_map_Agg.png", soc_map, width = 8, height = 6, dpi = 300)


```
